record.excerpt: So I took the pure long-side Turtle code — 20-day breakout, 10-day exit, ATR stops — and let it loose on: … Including: Bitcoin & Ethereum … Buy when price breaks above the highest high of the last 20 days. … Exit when price reverses direction for 10 days. … 18 years of data (2007-2025) … Total profit across all 43 markets: $1,147,318 … It's completely misleading.
record.notes: Turtle 20/10 Donchian long-only; result is pooled over 43 futures markets incl. BTC/ETH, so per-asset claim is not stated; author himself calls aggregate misleading.

spec.claim_summary: A long-only Turtle system that buys on a 20-day high breakout, exits on a 10-day low breakdown and uses ATR stops was run across 43 markets including Bitcoin and Ethereum.
assumptions: Timeframe 1d is assumed from day-based breakout/exit definitions and daily chart; the claim never states a bar timeframe.
Entry compiled as close > highest_high of previous 20 bars evaluated on bar close, filled at next open per engine convention.
Exit phrase interpreted as standard Turtle long Donchian exit: close < lowest_low of previous 10 bars.

NOT EXPRESSIBLE: The claim tests a 43-market portfolio for portfolio-level profit; the full 43-market list is not disclosed beyond Bitcoin & Ethereum and includes non-crypto markets outside engine data, so the test covers only the explicitly named BTCUSDT and ETHUSDT and cannot reproduce portfolio-level profit.

NOT EXPRESSIBLE: Turtle ATR stops are trailing ATR-based stops with position sizing/pyramiding; the schema has no entry-price-relative trailing ATR stop, so the trailing and sizing logic is omitted and approximated as a fixed stop_loss_pct.

evidence.quote: Buy when price breaks above the highest high of the last 20 days.
Exit when price reverses direction for 10 days.

issues.problem: Claim tests a 43-market portfolio for $1,147,318 total profit; spec tests only BTCUSDT and ETHUSDT. Omitting 41 markets means the portfolio-level result cannot be reproduced and changes what is being tested.
Claim states only 'ATR stops' with no percent value; spec invents a fixed 5.0% stop and omits trailing ATR logic. Invented threshold changes what is tested.
Claim gives no stop-size grid; spec invents candidates 2.0, 5.0, 8.0, 12.0 for stop_loss_pct. Invented optimization grid changes what is tested.
Claim tests 43 markets for Total profit across all 43 markets: $1,147,318 Including: Bitcoin & Ethereum. Spec tests only BTCUSDT and ETHUSDT subset, which cannot reproduce portfolio-level profit.

report.headline: Tested an approximation of the claim. Holds up: +13.81% per trade after costs over 50 trades, beats random timing (p = 0.015).
warnings: the claim's results start 2007-01-01; Binance history for BTCUSDT starts 2017-08-17, so the test covers less history than the claim
too few trades after the claim's period to judge it out-of-sample
